venueLine2: Campus Ministry to the University of Colorado
audienceNote: Open to University of Colorado students, high schoolers, and members of neighboring Lutheran congregations.
adultHeadline: Stand with the students who are *standing for their faith.*
adultSubhead: University Lutheran Chapel is starting a Champions for Religious Liberty chapter — and the students who host it are asking their neighbors to sit at the table with them.
studentHeadline: Hold your ground. *You don't have to hold it alone.*
studentSubhead: A Champions for Religious Liberty chapter at ULC — ten Thursday evenings to get equipped, and neighbors from around Boulder standing beside you.
conferenceNote: Rev. Mark Frith speaks at the ULC conference on September 19.

posterColumns.title: Why the students need you
paras: A university campus is a lonely place to hold a biblical conviction — in the lecture hall, in the dorm, in conversations our students didn't choose.
They host this chapter. But a student's calendar is rarely their own, and a chapter of students alone empties out at midterms. **Members of neighboring congregations are what make it hold.**
The ask is simple: ten evenings on your calendar, and a seat in the room.

posterColumns.title: And you'll be equipped too
paras: The Champions Academy trains ordinary Christians to speak clearly about religious liberty — distinguishing God's **left-hand kingdom** from His **right-hand kingdom**, engaging the culture with humility rather than heat.
Ten guided evenings on life, marriage, education, and the First Amendment. No prior study required.

audienceA.handoutLead: A student's calendar is rarely their own. A chapter made only of students empties out at midterms — and the handful still in the room lose heart. **Your presence is what makes it hold.**

bullets.text: Be the ones who show up every time, so the students are never the only ones in the room.
Two-kingdom thinking, the First Amendment, life, marriage, and education.
What you learn here, you carry back into your own congregation.
